modules.title: Computer files browsers and a learning workspace
modules.practice: Create folders for notes, code and evidence. Save a plain text file, rename it, find it again, download a course handout and distinguish a URL from a local path. In Scratch, build a small branching programme from the lecture.
modules.assessment: Without a walkthrough, recreate the folder structure, save and reopen a text file, locate a downloaded handout, and explain source code versus a running programme.
modules.pass_criteria: Complete all file operations independently and show the working Scratch programme.
modules.note: A computer, browser, internet connection and ability to read the teaching language are the entry requirements. Use the lecture to introduce unfamiliar computing terms; later modules revisit binary and programming in detail.

modules.title: Security goals ethics and authorised practice
modules.practice: Write a one-page scope for a fictional family document-sharing service: assets, permitted test environment, excluded real accounts, stop conditions and how evidence is recorded. Read the pwn.college environment instructions; the first command-line practical occurs in L01 after shell instruction.
modules.assessment: Classify ten self-written scenarios by confidentiality, integrity or availability and identify which activities fall outside the written scope.
modules.pass_criteria: Correctly classify at least eight scenarios and identify every action outside scope. Explain why permission for one system does not cover another.
modules.note: Practical security work in this map is confined to designated training environments or systems you own and explicitly choose for practice. Do not use personal or employer secrets as lab data.

modules.title: Accounts devices backups and personal privacy
modules.practice: Use a test account to document strong authentication and a recovery procedure. Create a harmless document, back it up, delete the working copy and restore it. Review update and screen-lock settings without changing organisational policy.
modules.assessment: Produce an account-recovery and lost-device checklist, restore a second file independently, and explain the difference between phishing resistance, encryption and backup.
modules.pass_criteria: Successful restoration with matching content; no secrets in the evidence; explain three distinct failure scenarios and suitable controls.

modules.title: Arithmetic algebra binary and encodings

readings.label: OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e contents — chapters 1 and 2

modules.practice: Work through OpenStax sections 1.1–1.10 and 2.1–2.4 as needed; do five exercises per unfamiliar section. On paper convert 13 and 255 to binary, 255 to hex, and explain bits versus bytes. Calculate 20 percent of 250, solve 3x+2=17, and evaluate powers and base-two logarithms.
modules.assessment: Independently solve equivalent problems with 19, 127, 15 percent of 360, 5x−4=26, 2^10, log2(64), and a bytes-to-bits conversion; explain why a text character can use more than one byte.
modules.pass_criteria: All representation and unit-conversion answers correct; at least 80 percent of algebra exercises correct. Repeat the relevant OpenStax section before proceeding if not.
modules.note: This is an explicit school-mathematics bridge. It can take several weeks when arithmetic or algebra is unfamiliar; no calculus is assumed.

modules.title: Python variables functions and input
modules.practice: Complete CS50P Problem Set 0, selecting Indoor Voice, Playback Speed and Making Faces from the linked assignment. Then write a function that converts a supplied number of bytes to bits and returns the result.
modules.assessment: Write a fresh command-line unit converter without copying an example and explain parameter, argument, return value and printed output.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct results for zero, positive and fractional inputs allowed by your specification; explain every line.
modules.note: The lecture page links Problem Set 0 and setup guidance. A hosted coding account may be required for official grading; local practice remains possible.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 0

modules.title: Conditions loops and algorithm tracing
modules.practice: Complete CS50P Deep Thought and Coke Machine from Problem Sets 1 and 2. Trace a loop by hand and write a bounded retry loop that stops after three invalid inputs.
modules.assessment: Create a small menu-driven programme with validation, cancellation and a retry limit; predict its output for six supplied input sequences.
modules.pass_criteria: All six traces match execution; cancellation terminates; invalid input never causes an infinite loop.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 1
Problem Set 2

modules.title: Collections exceptions and data modelling
modules.practice: Complete CS50P Grocery List and Fuel Gauge. Build a dictionary counting fictional login outcomes; deliberately include empty and malformed records.
modules.assessment: Count successes and failures per user from a new in-memory dataset and explain the treatment of malformed entries.
modules.pass_criteria: Exact counts on a hand-checked dataset; malformed entries are reported rather than silently discarded or crashing the programme.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 2
Problem Set 3

modules.title: Modules files CSV JSON and time

readings.label: Python datetime documentation — aware and naive objects

modules.practice: Complete CS50P Lines of Code and Pizza Py. Write a programme that reads a synthetic CSV with user, timestamp and outcome columns, validates rows, and writes JSON. Read the datetime sections on aware timestamps and ISO formats.
modules.assessment: Convert a new CSV containing missing fields and timestamps with two explicit UTC offsets into normalised UTC JSON.
modules.pass_criteria: Preserve valid records and field meanings, account for every rejected row, and correctly order events across the offsets.
modules.note: JSON is a data format, not executable code. The exercises use synthetic records created by the learner.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 6

modules.title: Tests debugging and regular expressions
modules.practice: Complete CS50P Testing my twttr and NUMB3RS. Add tests for valid, malformed, empty and boundary inputs in the CSV programme. Record one defect, its cause and a regression test.
modules.assessment: Given a deliberately flawed validation function you write on a separate day, identify the error with a failing test and fix it without weakening the test.
modules.pass_criteria: Show a meaningful test failing before the fix and passing afterward; cover at least six distinct edge cases; explain regex limitations.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 5
Problem Set 7

modules.title: Linux shell paths documentation and files

videos.label: MIT Course Overview and The Shell lecture

readings.label: MIT The Shell reading and exercises
Linux Luminarium — Hello Hackers Pondering Paths and Comprehending Commands

modules.practice: In the pwn.college browser workspace complete Hello Hackers, Pondering Paths, Comprehending Commands and Digesting Documentation. Recreate the O01 folder exercise using shell commands.
modules.assessment: Navigate a fresh directory tree, locate a named file, inspect its type and contents, and explain an absolute path, a relative path and the current directory.
modules.pass_criteria: Complete the navigation without a copied command sequence; justify each command and recover from one incorrect path.

modules.title: Permissions processes pipes environment and shell scripting

videos.label: MIT Shell Tools and Scripting lecture

readings.label: MIT Shell Tools and Scripting reading
Linux Luminarium — Practicing Piping Shell Variables Processes and Jobs Untangling Users Perceiving Permissions

modules.practice: Complete the named Linux Luminarium modules. Write a shell pipeline that counts outcomes in a synthetic log, demonstrate redirection, and inspect your own processes and environment. Use only your lab account for permission changes.
modules.assessment: Independently create an owner-only directory and readable report, safely handle a filename containing spaces, and stop only the background process you launched.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct permissions and counts; no unintended process terminated; explain quoting, PATH and why a pipe passes output to input.

modules.title: Objects dependency environments and reproducible Python

readings.label: Python tutorial Virtual Environments and Packages

modules.practice: Model validated log records using a class. Create a virtual environment, install only a needed package from its documented source if one is required, record versions, and rebuild the environment. Use JSON for untrusted data rather than pickle.
modules.assessment: Recreate the programme in a clean environment from written instructions and reject malformed records at the class boundary.
modules.pass_criteria: A second person or a clean environment reproduces the result; installation and input assumptions are written down; class validation has tests.
modules.note: The MIT lesson page contains its embedded lecture. Build tools mentioned only as examples do not need to be installed.

modules.title: Git version history and a reproducible lab notebook

readings.label: MIT Version Control reading and exercises

modules.practice: Create a local repository for harmless practice code. Make two commits, a feature branch and a merge; inspect differences. Add a README with environment, input and reproduction instructions. Keep credentials and personal data out of Git.
modules.assessment: Recreate a past programme version, explain its diff, and reproduce the P04 output from a fresh checkout.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct history and output; a reader can follow the README; all dependencies are recorded.

modules.title: Logic sets functions proofs graphs and state machines

videos.label: Lecture 11: Relations, Partial Orders, and Scheduling

readings.label: Learn TLA — introduction and mathematical prerequisites

modules.practice: Write truth tables for AND, OR and implication; model user-to-role membership as sets; draw a login state machine; prove a simple loop invariant by induction. Work the corresponding examples in the assigned chapters.
modules.assessment: Distinguish a claim from its converse, give a counterexample to an invalid implication, and prove that a bounded retry counter never exceeds its limit.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct truth tables and counterexample; a proof with base case and inductive step; a state diagram with explicit transitions.
modules.note: The 2010 MIT notes omit their state-machine chapter. Learn TLA supplies that bridge; do not assign the missing chapter.

modules.title: Modular arithmetic number theory and counting

readings.label: Boneh Shoup version 0.6 — appendix A Basic number theory

modules.practice: Compute gcd(35,64), the inverse of 3 modulo 11, and small modular powers. Count fixed-length strings over specified alphabets and compare linear, polynomial and exponential growth.
modules.assessment: Solve equivalent unseen modular-inverse and counting problems and explain when an inverse does not exist.
modules.pass_criteria: All modular calculations verified by substitution; counting assumptions explicit; distinguish combinations from ordered sequences.

modules.title: Probability independence entropy and the base rate
modules.practice: Calculate the posterior probability of a real incident when prevalence is 1 percent, sensitivity 90 percent and false-positive rate 5 percent. Simulate fair dice using Python random and compare averages to expectation. Estimate guessing work for uniformly selected strings.
modules.assessment: Recalculate with different prevalence and error rates; explain why high sensitivity alone does not make most alerts true and why human password choice is not uniform.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct conditional probability with denominators shown; distinguish independence from mutual exclusion; separate a simulation result from a proof.

modules.title: Statistics sampling uncertainty and experimental design

videos.label: Population and Estimated Parameters, Clearly Explained
Estimating the Mean, Variance and Standard Deviation
Hypothesis Testing and the Null Hypothesis
p-values: What they are and how to interpret them
Machine Learning Fundamentals: Sensitivity and Specificity

readings.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e — sections 1.1 through 1.4 2.5 2.7 8.1 and 9.1 through 9.4

modules.practice: Compute mean and sample variance for harmless synthetic response times. Build a hand-checked confusion matrix, calculate precision and recall, then compare two simple offline rule variants on a fixed synthetic dataset. Explain sampling assumptions.
modules.assessment: Write a preregistered comparison specifying the question, dataset split, metric, repetitions and uncertainty before examining results; critique one misleading p-value claim.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct calculations, no test-data tuning, clear unit of analysis and justified uncertainty. Identify at least two confounders.
modules.note: This is calculus-free preparation for evaluating security claims.

modules.title: C compilation types and machine representation
modules.practice: Compile the lecture hello-world example and a byte-conversion programme. Inspect compiler warnings, return codes, integer limits and an explicitly checked input range.
modules.assessment: Write and compile a fresh C conversion function that rejects out-of-range input and explain the source-to-executable steps.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct boundary behaviour, no ignored relevant warnings, and an accurate explanation of compile time versus run time.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 1

modules.title: Arrays strings encodings and bounds
modules.practice: Complete CS50x Readability or a comparable text counter from the assignment. Write a bounded string-copy routine for learning, testing empty, exact-fit and too-long input. Distinguish byte length from character count.
modules.assessment: Explain the memory occupied by a small string and implement a validator with explicit buffer capacity.
modules.pass_criteria: All boundary cases handled, a terminator accounted for, and no claim that byte count always equals character count.

practice_links.label: Problem Set 2

modules.title: Algorithms data structures recursion and complexity

readings.label: MIT 2010 course notes — chapter 9 Sums and asymptotics

modules.practice: Implement a simple lookup using a list and then a dictionary or hash table. Trace binary search and recursion; measure operation counts rather than drawing conclusions from one timing measurement.
modules.assessment: Choose structures for a user lookup and an ordered event stream, justify the choice and state worst-case versus expected behaviour.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct implementation and termination; defensible complexity statements; explain the cost of a hash collision without assuming all operations are constant time.

modules.title: Pointers allocation stack heap linked structures and debugging
skills: linked lists hash table implementation and trees
modules.practice: Draw stack and heap layouts for two small C functions. Allocate and release a buffer, then use a debugger to inspect addresses and a compiler memory-safety diagnostic on deliberately incorrect lab code. After pointer practice, watch the data-structures lecture and implement a two-node linked list with explicit allocation and cleanup.
modules.assessment: Fix an out-of-bounds access and a lifetime error in your own benign programme, retaining tests that expose each defect. Explain the pointer links and cleanup of the list.
modules.pass_criteria: Explain ownership and lifetime, show the original failing evidence and corrected behaviour, and release all owned allocations.

modules.title: Assembly calling conventions executables and debuggers

videos.label: Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 2 x86 Assembly and Call Stack

readings.label: pwn.college Computing 101 — Your First Program Computer Memory The Stack Software Introspection and Debugging Refresher

modules.practice: Complete the named Computing 101 modules in order, using their embedded explanations. Compile a small benign C programme, disassemble it, break at a function and relate registers and stack values to source variables.
modules.assessment: Explain a new short disassembly, locate a parameter and return value, and identify where a function returns.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct register and stack explanation; distinguish executable file layout from live process memory.
modules.note: Use the Linux x86 training environment supplied by pwn.college when your own machine has a different CPU. Hardware emulation and installation are not assumed.

modules.title: Operating systems privilege virtual memory and filesystems
skills: processes system calls kernel user mode
modules.practice: In a lab, inspect a process and its open files. Trace one benign file operation at the system-call boundary. Draw virtual-to-physical address translation conceptually and inspect file permissions, timestamps and directory entries.
modules.assessment: Explain why two processes may use the same virtual address without sharing data, and distinguish a filename, directory entry, file contents and process handle.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct privilege boundary and address-space explanations; correctly identify which metadata an ordinary file copy may change.

modules.title: Threads concurrency locks races and deadlocks
modules.practice: Work the MIT worksheet before opening answers. Model a two-worker counter as explicit read-modify-write steps and enumerate an interleaving that loses an update. Add a lock and analyse a two-lock deadlock.
modules.assessment: Prove or refute an atomicity claim for a fresh transfer scenario and propose a locking order.
modules.pass_criteria: A concrete failing interleaving, a valid fix and a deadlock argument. A run that happens to succeed is insufficient evidence of thread safety.

modules.title: Networks layers packets and performance

videos.label: Kurose Ross 1.1 What is the Internet

modules.practice: Complete the Wireshark introductory lab using supplied traces where capture permissions or hardware are unavailable. Draw encapsulation and compute transmission time for a stated byte count and link rate.
modules.assessment: Identify the network layers and endpoints in a fresh capture and distinguish throughput, bandwidth and latency.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct layer mapping and units; explain what packet capture can and cannot observe.
modules.note: The first PDF on the Wireshark page is its introductory v9 lab. Use only your own traffic or supplied educational traces.

modules.title: IP addressing subnetting routing NAT and IPv6

readings.label: Wireshark labs — IP v9 and NAT v9

modules.practice: Work the IP and NAT labs using supplied traces. Calculate network membership for /24 and /26 examples, draw a three-subnet network and explain its routing choices.
modules.assessment: Assign non-overlapping subnets to three fictional departments and trace a packet through NAT and a default route.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct subnet ranges and routes; explain why address translation alone does not establish an access-control policy.

modules.title: Ethernet ARP DHCP and wireless security foundations

readings.label: Wireshark Ethernet and ARP v9 DHCP v9 and 802.11 v9 labs

modules.practice: Inspect the ARP and DHCP educational traces and identify request, response and assigned configuration. Use the supplied wireless trace for association analysis rather than requiring a monitor-mode wireless adapter.
modules.assessment: Explain a fresh host-joins-LAN sequence and identify what changes when a destination is on another subnet.
modules.pass_criteria: Correctly distinguish MAC from IP addresses, ARP from DNS, and wireless encryption from end-to-end application encryption.

modules.title: TCP UDP reliable delivery and socket programming

videos.label: Kurose Ross 3.4 Reliable data transfer part 1
Kurose Ross 3.4 Reliable data transfer part 2

readings.label: Wireshark TCP v9 and UDP v9 labs

modules.practice: Complete the TCP and UDP trace labs. Write a Python loopback echo client and server with a bounded message length and timeout; observe a closed port and an incomplete message.
modules.assessment: Explain a TCP handshake, retransmission and connection close from a new trace; distinguish a byte stream from application message framing.
modules.pass_criteria: Working bounded echo programme; correct packet interpretation; no assumption that one recv call returns an entire application message.

modules.title: DNS email and name-resolution trust

videos.label: Kurose Ross 2.4 The Domain Name Service DNS

modules.practice: Complete the DNS trace lab and follow a fictional email path. Compare authoritative answers, cached answers and mail-exchange records. Read the conceptual DNSSEC section without implementing a resolver.
modules.assessment: Diagnose whether a fictional outage is caused by name resolution, transport or application behaviour and explain the evidence.
modules.pass_criteria: Accurately interpret A AAAA MX and CNAME records; distinguish DNS authenticity from traffic confidentiality.

modules.title: HTTP requests responses cookies caches and proxies
skills: HTTP versions reverse proxies cache keys

videos.label: Kurose Ross 2.2 Web and HTTP part 1
Kurose Ross 2.2 Web and HTTP part 2

modules.practice: Complete the HTTP trace lab. Use browser developer tools on a harmless page to identify method, path, status, headers, body and cookies. Draw a client, reverse proxy, cache and origin server.
modules.assessment: Explain a fresh request-response transcript and predict whether two requests should share a cache entry.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct transcript parsing and cache assumptions; distinguish transport connection state from an application login session.

modules.title: HTML JavaScript DOM forms and origins
modules.practice: Create a local static form with a small JavaScript event handler. Use developer tools to inspect DOM nodes and requests. Compare origins for URLs differing in scheme, hostname and port.
modules.assessment: Build a new form from a written specification, explain which code executes in the browser, and correctly classify ten same-origin pairs.
modules.pass_criteria: Working form and handler; all origin comparisons correct; understand that client-side checks can be changed by the client.

modules.title: Relational databases SQL schemas and transactions
modules.practice: Create a local SQLite database for users and notes. Write joins and updates, add an ownership relationship, and demonstrate rollback of a failed transfer. Follow the course examples for parameter binding.
modules.assessment: Answer five new queries and implement an all-or-nothing update with negative tests for missing and duplicate data.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct rows and constraints; rollback preserves the invariant; data values are passed separately from SQL syntax.

modules.title: Web servers APIs sessions and structured data

readings.label: MDN XML introduction — structure and entities

modules.practice: Build a local Flask notes app using SQLite, two fictional users, a session cookie and a small JSON endpoint. Add explicit ownership checks and server-side validation. Read a small XML example and identify its document type and entity declarations conceptually.
modules.assessment: Implement a second endpoint from a specification; explain every trust boundary and test that one user cannot read another user’s note.
modules.pass_criteria: Positive and negative authorisation tests pass; HTTP requests and JSON are traceable to server code; no real credentials used.
modules.note: This original practice app becomes the defensive assessment target later. It is kept local until deliberately deployed under a separate decision.

modules.title: Virtual machines containers snapshots and lab isolation

readings.label: Docker overview — architecture images containers networking and storage
SEED Labs 20.04 catalogue and environment instructions

modules.practice: Choose a documented lab environment suited to the host architecture. Run only a benign container first; map its process, ports and storage. Create and restore a snapshot or rebuild from the recorded image. Document how the vulnerable app is restricted to the lab.
modules.assessment: Rebuild the environment independently, demonstrate the expected reachable ports and show that resetting removes a harmless change.
modules.pass_criteria: Reproducible reset, documented architecture and image versions, and no unintended exposure of the vulnerable app.
modules.note: Browser-hosted labs remain an alternative for exercises that support them. Windows and x86 specialist labs may need a separate compatible VM; later modules state that requirement explicitly.

modules.title: Threat modelling secure design and security principles

videos.label: Lecture 2: threat models and security policies

modules.practice: Threat-model the notes app: assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, attacker capabilities, security goals and out-of-scope assumptions. Propose controls tied to each threat.
modules.assessment: Review a changed design that adds file sharing and revise the threat model without simply adding more controls.
modules.pass_criteria: Every control addresses an explicit threat; identify at least one residual risk and one usability or operational tradeoff.

modules.title: Symmetric encryption randomness and authenticated encryption

videos.label: Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 12 Symmetric Key Encryption
Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 13 Symmetric Key Encryption continued

modules.practice: Use a maintained cryptographic library in the lab to encrypt and decrypt a harmless message with an authenticated-encryption API. Change the ciphertext and verify rejection. Compare cryptographic randomness with seeded simulation randomness.
modules.assessment: Design a message format with a nonce and tag, reject a modified message and explain nonce uniqueness requirements for the selected construction.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct round trip and tamper rejection; no custom cipher; clear key and nonce handling.
modules.note: Follow the selected library’s current documentation for its API. Toy cryptography in the readings is for reasoning rather than deployment. Authenticated encryption is first used through its library API; S03 supplies MAC definitions and the construction-level explanation.

modules.title: Hashes MACs password storage and key derivation

videos.label: Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 7 Authentication and Cryptographic Hashes

modules.practice: Hash two harmless files, authenticate a message using a library MAC, and store two identical test passwords using a recommended password-hashing API with distinct salts. Verify negative cases.
modules.assessment: Choose encryption, hashing, MAC or password hashing for five new scenarios and justify each choice.
modules.pass_criteria: All five choices defensible; modified MAC rejected; explain why a fast unsalted hash is unsuitable for password storage.

modules.title: Public keys key exchange signatures and certificates

videos.label: Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 15 Key Exchange and Public Key Encryption
Berkeley CS161 2026 Lecture 10 Public Key Infrastructure

modules.practice: Work a small-number Diffie–Hellman example by hand, then use a standard library to sign and verify a harmless document. Inspect an ordinary site certificate and identify issuer, subject, validity and name constraints.
modules.assessment: Explain an active interception of unauthenticated key exchange and propose a certificate or pre-established trust solution.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct small-number exchange and signature rejection for changed data; explain the trust anchor and the difference between a signature and encryption.

modules.title: TLS HTTPS and secure network protocols
modules.practice: Complete the TLS trace lab and annotate which parts remain visible on the network. Use the local app or a controlled example to show that hostname verification rejects the wrong peer.
modules.assessment: Explain a fresh HTTPS flow and list attacks that remain possible despite transport encryption.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct handshake and trust explanation; do not disable certificate validation as a fix.
modules.note: MIT Lecture 14 uses historical SSL and TLS examples. The Berkeley reading and RFC 8446 supply current TLS 1.3 context.

modules.title: Authentication authorisation sessions and least privilege
modules.practice: Write a role-and-object access matrix for the notes app. Implement session expiry and owner checks using framework facilities. Enumerate account-recovery and administrator paths as part of the threat model.
modules.assessment: Test every allow and deny cell of a fresh access matrix, including logged-out users and changed object identifiers.
modules.pass_criteria: No unauthorised path succeeds; session and recovery assumptions explicit; distinguish identity proof from permission to act.

modules.title: Browser developer tools and intercepting HTTP

videos.label: Kurose Ross 2.2 Web and HTTP part 1

readings.label: OWASP WSTG stable — introduction and testing framework

modules.practice: Follow the Burp getting-started tutorial with its supplied browser and demonstration target. Intercept, inspect and repeat one harmless request; compare request and response headers. Keep a separate lab browser profile.
modules.assessment: Inspect an unfamiliar request from the local notes app and identify cookies, method, body encoding and response status without changing production traffic.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct transcript and repeatable capture procedure; explain why trusting a lab proxy certificate changes the lab browser trust boundary.

modules.title: SQL injection and parameterised queries

videos.label: Intigriti — SQL Injection to Retrieve Hidden Data!

readings.label: PortSwigger SQL injection — overview examples and prevention

modules.practice: Complete the guided lab SQL injection vulnerability in WHERE clause allowing retrieval of hidden data, then replace a deliberately concatenated query in a local toy endpoint with bound parameters.
modules.assessment: Complete the different lab SQL injection vulnerability allowing login bypass without its solution, then write positive and negative tests for a corrected local query.
modules.pass_criteria: Solve the fresh lab, explain the query change, and demonstrate that the fix rejects injection while preserving legitimate apostrophes and ordinary input.
modules.note: The guided video is a community demonstration embedded by PortSwigger. Independent lab: https://portswigger.net/web-security/sql-injection/lab-login-bypass

videos.label: z3nsh3ll — What is Reflected XSS? (Cross Site Scripting)
z3nsh3ll — What Is Stored XSS? (Cross Site Scripting)

readings.label: PortSwigger XSS — reflected stored DOM contexts and prevention

modules.practice: Complete Reflected XSS into HTML context with nothing encoded and Stored XSS into HTML context with nothing encoded. Fix the corresponding local template or DOM sink using context-appropriate escaping or text-only APIs.
modules.assessment: Review three fresh sinks: HTML text, an attribute and a DOM assignment. Identify which inputs reach executable contexts and write tests for the safe alternatives.
modules.pass_criteria: All three contexts explained; executable input becomes inert without breaking ordinary text; distinguish CSP mitigation from removing an unsafe sink.

practice_links.label: Lab: Reflected XSS into HTML context with nothing encoded
Lab: Stored XSS into HTML context with nothing encoded

modules.title: Cross site request forgery and session boundaries

videos.label: Intigriti — How To Search For CSRF!

readings.label: PortSwigger CSRF — how it works and prevention

modules.assessment: Design and test protection for a different state-changing endpoint, including a legitimate submission and a cross-origin request.
modules.pass_criteria: Negative requests fail and legitimate requests succeed; explain why changing a request to POST alone does not prevent CSRF.

practice_links.label: Lab: CSRF vulnerability with no defenses

modules.title: Same origin policy CORS and cross origin access

videos.label: Rana Khalil — CORS - Lab #1 CORS vulnerability with basic origin reflection | Short Video

readings.label: PortSwigger CORS — browser enforcement and misconfigurations

modules.practice: Complete CORS vulnerability with basic origin reflection. Build an explicit local origin allowlist and inspect a preflight request with the lab browser.
modules.assessment: Predict which of six origin-and-credentials combinations a proposed policy permits, then verify them against the local configuration.
modules.pass_criteria: All six predictions correct; reject untrusted origins; distinguish a browser read restriction from server-side authorisation.

practice_links.label: Lab: CORS vulnerability with basic origin reflection

modules.title: Path traversal and filesystem boundaries

videos.label: Rana Khalil — Directory Traversal - Lab #1 File path traversal, simple case | Short Version

readings.label: PortSwigger Path traversal — examples and prevention

modules.practice: Complete File path traversal simple case. In a harmless local file viewer, replace user-supplied paths with an allowlisted identifier-to-file mapping; test normal and traversal-like inputs.
modules.assessment: Evaluate a different download design with nested paths and symlinks and explain its containment assumptions.
modules.pass_criteria: No escape from the intended directory in tested cases; legitimate files remain accessible; document symlink and platform assumptions.

practice_links.label: Lab: File path traversal, simple case

modules.title: OS command injection and process invocation

videos.label: Rana Khalil — Command Injection - Lab #1 OS command injection, simple case | Short Version

readings.label: PortSwigger OS command injection — simple cases and prevention

modules.practice: Complete OS command injection simple case. Refactor a local utility wrapper to pass a fixed executable and explicit argument list without shell interpolation. Use only harmless commands and test data.
modules.assessment: Explain the handling of spaces, quotes and leading option characters in a new wrapper design; add regression tests.
modules.pass_criteria: Correct argument boundaries and option handling; no shell-string concatenation; explain why a blacklist of metacharacters is incomplete.

practice_links.label: Lab: OS command injection, simple case

modules.title: File upload validation storage and execution boundaries

videos.label: Intigriti — How File Upload Vulnerabilities Work!

readings.label: PortSwigger File upload vulnerabilities — causes and prevention

modules.practice: Complete Remote code execution via web shell upload only in the supplied lab. Build a local harmless text-upload endpoint using generated storage names, a size limit, an allowlist and storage outside executable content paths.
modules.assessment: Test double extensions, mismatched content types, oversized input, duplicate names and unauthorised retrieval against your local endpoint.
modules.pass_criteria: Every negative case is rejected or safely stored as inert data; legitimate uploads work; explain server-side execution and download access controls.

practice_links.label: Lab: Remote code execution via web shell upload

modules.title: XML parsers external entities and safe data handling

videos.label: Seven Seas Security — XXE Lab Breakdown: Exploiting XXE using external entities to retrieve files

readings.label: PortSwigger XXE — external entities attack surface and prevention

modules.assessment: Compare a parser that permits external entities with the corrected configuration using a harmless local marker file and a blocked network reference.
modules.pass_criteria: Legitimate XML still parses; external access is blocked; document whether DTDs, entity expansion and network access are disabled.

practice_links.label: Lab: Exploiting XXE using external entities to retrieve files

modules.title: Server side request forgery and outbound trust

videos.label: Rana Khalil — SSRF - Lab #1 Basic SSRF against the local server | Short Version

readings.label: PortSwigger SSRF — local server backends and prevention
